title: The Permutation-Descent Model of the Eulerian Numbers: Non-negativity and ∑ₖ ⟨n,k⟩ = n!
description: Settles the non-negativity half of the parent's open question and builds the missing combinatorial object for the descent interpretation of the Eulerian numbers. eulerianExplicit_nonneg proves the alternating inclusion–exclusion sum ∑_{i=0}^{k} (−1)ⁱ·C(n+1,i)·(k+1−i)ⁿ ≥ 0, immediately from the parent's identity with the recurrence-defined ⟨n,k⟩ (a count). A from-scratch permutation-descent statistic numDescents on Equiv.Perm (Fin n) — read off the value sequence σ 0, σ 1, …, σ(n−1) via the list helper listDes — and the counting function eulerianDesc n k = #{σ | numDescents σ = k} are defined; Mathlib contains neither. The headline structural result sum_eulerianDesc_eq_factorial proves ∑_{k=0}^{n} eulerianDesc n k = n!, i.e. the descent statistic partitions the symmetric group, via Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise once descents are bounded by n (numDescents_le), together with Fintype.card_perm and Fintype.card_fin. The identification eulerianDesc = eulerian (the full descent interpretation) requires the Eulerian insertion bijection and is recorded as the remaining open continuation; agreement is decide-confirmed on row n=3. 122 lines, 4 theorems, 3 definitions, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

overview.historicalContext: The Eulerian numbers ⟨n,k⟩ classically count the permutations of {1,…,n} with exactly k descents — positions i where σ(i) > σ(i+1). This descent interpretation is their original combinatorial meaning (Euler, 1755; Graham–Knuth–Patashnik, Concrete Mathematics §6.2). The parent entry built ⟨n,k⟩ from the triangle recurrence and proved the explicit inclusion–exclusion formula; its open question asks to connect that recurrence-defined integer back to its descent meaning and to deduce non-negativity. Mathlib has no descent statistic on permutations and no Eulerian numbers in any form, so the combinatorial object underlying the descent interpretation must be built from scratch.
overview.problemStatement: Using the parent's explicit formula and the recurrence-defined Eulerian numbers ⟨n,k⟩, (1) prove the alternating sum eulerianExplicit n k is non-negative, and (2) build the permutation-descent counting function eulerianDesc n k = #{σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) | descents σ = k} and establish that the descent statistic is a genuine statistic on Sₙ, namely ∑_{k=0}^{n} eulerianDesc n k = n!. All with 0 axioms and 0 sorries.
overview.proofStrategy: Non-negativity is immediate: by the parent's eulerian_eq_explicit, eulerianExplicit n k equals the natural-number count ⟨n,k⟩, so it is ≥ 0 by exact_mod_cast. For the descent model, define listDes recursively on lists of naturals (counting adjacent strict descents), set numDescents σ = listDes (List.ofFn (σ ·)), and eulerianDesc n k as the cardinality of the descent-k fibre of Equiv.Perm (Fin n). Prove listDes_le_length (descents ≤ length) by a two-step list induction, giving numDescents_le : numDescents σ ≤ n via List.length_ofFn. Then the descent statistic maps Sₙ into range (n+1), so Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise partitions #(Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) over the descent value; rewriting with Fintype.card_perm and Fintype.card_fin turns the left side into n!.
keyInsights: Non-negativity of the daunting alternating inclusion–exclusion sum is free once the parent's recurrence/explicit identification is in hand: the sum IS a natural-number count, so its sign is automatic — no direct sign analysis of the alternating terms is needed.

Reading descents off the value sequence via List.ofFn and a tiny recursive list counter (listDes) sidesteps the dependent-index pain of comparing σ at consecutive Fin n positions, and stays fully decidable so small rows are decide-checkable.

The partition identity ∑ₖ eulerianDesc n k = n! is exactly Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise applied to the descent statistic: it says descents are a well-defined statistic whose fibres tile Sₙ, the structural prerequisite for the descent interpretation.

The bound numDescents σ ≤ n (a permutation of n+1 values has at most n descents, and listDes l ≤ l.length) is what licenses summing over the finite range (n+1) — without it the fiberwise partition has no finite index set.

meta.author: Lean Genius
originalContributions: numDescents / listDes: a from-scratch permutation-descent statistic on Equiv.Perm (Fin n), counting positions where the value sequence σ 0, σ 1, …, σ(n−1) strictly decreases. Mathlib has no descent statistic on permutations; this is the combinatorial object underlying the descent interpretation of the Eulerian numbers.

eulerianDesc: the Eulerian number realized as a descent count, eulerianDesc n k = #{σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) | numDescents σ = k}. This is the object the parent's open question asks to connect to ⟨n,k⟩.

sum_eulerianDesc_eq_factorial: THE MAIN STRUCTURAL RESULT — the descent statistic partitions the symmetric group, ∑_{k=0}^{n} eulerianDesc n k = n!. Proved by Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise applied to the descent statistic (bounded by numDescents_le), with Fintype.card_perm and Fintype.card_fin evaluating #(Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) = n!.

eulerianExplicit_nonneg: 0 ≤ ∑_{i=0}^{k} (−1)ⁱ·C(n+1,i)·(k+1−i)ⁿ — the non-negativity half of the parent's open question — obtained directly from the parent's identification of the alternating sum with the natural-number count ⟨n,k⟩.

numDescents_le / listDes_le_length: a permutation of Fin n has at most n descents (and any list has at most length-many descents), the bound that lets the descent counts be summed over the finite range (n+1).
prerequisites: Parent: geometric-series-oq-07-oq-01-oq-01-oq-01-oq-02 (the explicit inclusion–exclusion formula) — supplies eulerianExplicit and eulerian_eq_explicit, used verbatim for non-negativity
Grandparent: geometric-series-oq-07-oq-01-oq-01-oq-01 (the combinatorial Eulerian numbers ⟨n,k⟩) reused via the parent

Mathlib's permutation/Fintype theory: Equiv.Perm (Fin n) as a Fintype, Fintype.card_perm (#(Equiv.Perm α) = (card α)!), Fintype.card_fin, and Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise for partitioning a Finset by the fibres of a map
Mathlib's List.ofFn / List.length_ofFn for reading a permutation's value sequence as a list

mathlibDependencies.description: Partitions the cardinality of a Finset over the fibres of a map into a finite index set: #s = ∑_{b ∈ t} #{a ∈ s | f a = b}, given the map sends s into t. Applied with f = numDescents, s = univ, t = range (n+1) to obtain the descent partition of Sₙ.
#(Equiv.Perm α) = (Fintype.card α)!. With α = Fin n and Fintype.card_fin this evaluates the order of the symmetric group to n!, the right-hand side of the descent partition identity.
(List.ofFn f).length = n. Combined with listDes_le_length it bounds the descent count of a permutation of Fin n by n, licensing the finite summation range.
The parent's identification (eulerian n k : ℤ) = eulerianExplicit n k. Rewriting by it turns non-negativity of the alternating sum into non-negativity of a natural-number cast.

openQuestions.question: Prove the full descent interpretation eulerianDesc n k = eulerian n k for all n,k by the Eulerian insertion bijection: inserting the largest value into a permutation of Fin n either preserves the descent count (k+1 positions) or raises it by one (n−k positions), yielding the triangle recurrence (k+2)·eulerianDesc n (k+1) + (n−k)·eulerianDesc n k. With the partition identity proved here this would complete the descent interpretation.

Prove the descent-count palindromy eulerianDesc n k = eulerianDesc n (n−1−k) directly by the reversal bijection σ ↦ σ ∘ rev, which exchanges descents and ascents, complementing the explicit-formula palindromy of the sibling oq-02-oq-02.

Sibling that proves Worpitzky's identity nᵐ = ∑ⱼ ⟨m,j⟩·C(n+j,m). Worpitzky is the algebraic shadow of the descent interpretation built here: it expands powers in the binomial basis with the Eulerian numbers as structure constants, the analytic counterpart to the permutation-descent count.

conclusion.summary: Building on the parent's explicit inclusion–exclusion formula for the combinatorial Eulerian numbers, this entry settles the non-negativity half of the parent's open question (eulerianExplicit_nonneg: the alternating sum equals the natural-number count ⟨n,k⟩, hence ≥ 0) and builds the missing combinatorial object for the descent interpretation: a from-scratch permutation-descent statistic numDescents on Equiv.Perm (Fin n) and the Eulerian-as-descent-count function eulerianDesc n k. Its headline result, sum_eulerianDesc_eq_factorial, proves the descent statistic partitions the symmetric group, ∑_{k=0}^{n} eulerianDesc n k = n!, via Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise (with the bound numDescents_le), Fintype.card_perm and Fintype.card_fin. 122 lines, 4 theorems, 3 definitions, 0 axioms, 0 sorries; everything depends only on propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
conclusion.implications: This establishes the descent statistic as a genuine statistic on the symmetric group and provides the combinatorial model the parent's open question asked for — Mathlib has neither the descent statistic nor the Eulerian numbers. The remaining step, the full identification eulerianDesc n k = eulerian n k, is the classical Eulerian insertion-bijection recurrence (recorded as a high-significance open continuation); together with the partition identity proved here it would complete the descent interpretation. Row n=3 agreement is decide-confirmed.
